plants.name: Rhododendron catawbiense
plants.description: Big rounded clusters of pink-to-purple blooms light up the evergreen shrubs on Appalachian slopes and balds. In full flower they look like waves of magenta rolling across the ridgelines.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, from about April to June. Blooming runs from late May into June, and the high-elevation peak comes around mid-June.
plants.location: Southern Appalachian Mountains, USA (Virginia through Georgia, including Roan Mountain on the North Carolina–Tennessee line)
plants.funFact: This native species is one of the parents of many of the hardy rhododendron hybrids grown in cold-climate gardens. Its tolerance of cold winters is a big reason for that.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all proteas, it has a flower head up to the size of a dinner plate. Its pink, silky-tipped bracts surround a crown of fuzzy florets. It blooms in the cool, misty Cape winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, roughly June to October in its homeland. In the Cape's cool season it is blooming around June 6.
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to an ancient plant family that dates back to the supercontinent Gondwana.
